sections.heading: Termites eat quietly. We look loudly.
sections.body:
Desert subterranean termites build mud tubes up your foundation and feed on framing from the inside out. By the time a wall sounds hollow, they have usually been there for years.

A licensed inspector checks the slab, the garage, the attic and the exterior line, and maps every tube and blister. If we find activity we treat with a non-repellent liquid barrier or a monitored bait system, and keep checking long after the bill is paid.

items.question: How do I know if I have termites?
items.answer: Look for pencil-width mud tubes on the foundation or garage walls, swarms of winged insects after a monsoon rain, and discarded wings on windowsills. A free inspection will confirm it either way.

items.question: Liquid treatment or bait stations?
items.answer: Liquid barriers act fast and protect the whole perimeter. Bait systems eliminate the colony over time with very little product. We recommend the right one after the inspection, and often combine them.

items.question: How long does a treatment last?
items.answer: A liquid barrier is typically effective for **five years or more**. Bait systems are monitored and serviced on a plan for as long as you keep it.

items.question: Do you do real estate inspections?
items.answer: Yes. Our licensed inspectors complete Wood Destroying Insect reports for buyers, sellers and lenders, usually within 48 hours.

items.question: Is there a warranty?
items.answer: Every termite treatment carries a renewable warranty. If termites return while it is active, we re-treat at no charge.
